newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds weaken as punt slips back vs the mark.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds weaken as punt slips back vs the mark.

text.p: Irish bonds weakened in late trade on Friday primarily due to selling pressure having forced the punt lower versus the mark but also because of weakness in international bond markets, dealers said.

"On the day today, we saw Irish bonds steady in the morning but slip back in the afternooon in line with international markets. German bunds in particular have lost ground versus T-notes while we have seen some selling of UK gilts as well," Riada's Padhraic Garvey said.

"The other big interest has been the forex market. The Irish pound opened stronger against the mark but met with selling pressure above 2.60 marks and that has pushed it down to around 2.5850. When the punt slips against the mark like that it is negative for Irish bonds," he addded.
By 1550 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down 30 pence at 102.20 to yield 5.90 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was down 35 pence at 109.55 to yield 6.58.
Dealers said Irish bonds had narrowed a couple of basis points against German bunds in the five-year area but were unchanged in terms of spreads against Germany in the 10-year area.
The Irish pound was at 2.5862/82 marks compared to 2.6015 marks at Thursday's close.

The main item of interest to the markets next week will be the meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on Tuesday as traders look for clues as to the future direction of U.S. interest rates, dealer said.
